chrome remains the canonical composition owner for the existing Qt window classes. Window flags/screen policy, title-bar appearance/controls, and the complete existing frameless interaction plus grips have distinct owners. The original mixin and Qt MRO are retained, not extended with shared-host helpers: drag/resize state stays solely on each window. Grip/titlebar QWidget parent references use interaction methods and do not duplicate geometry/state. Twelve reexports are exact aliases. Fifteen original top-level definitions/constants retain exact AST; FramelessWindowMixin changes only one local direction normalization, fixing camel-case corner grips that previously resized vertically only. Existing composition-level hooks and signal-time method lookup remain. Tests cover event super order, first-show centering, screen priority, state isolation and eight resize directions including minimum bounds. Native source inventory includes all three new production owners; no build/release qualification is claimed.

Production GUI discovery/configuration/attachment owner. It now inherits only StartupLifecycle, which owns cancellation, receipt and thread lifetime without backend/journal construction helpers. New dynamic tests trap execution owners anywhere in the GUI process.

Canonical service client with private transport lanes and one RemoteSessions publication store. Raw session publication methods are internal; immutable views derive from SessionPublication. Explicit control/recovery and detach semantics remain. No legacy backend authority crosses this interface.

LiveModelSession remains the sole current owner of session state, locks, scheduling and event history. Only protocol constants/error/decoder and message parsers are compatibility imports from stateless owners. Runner result projection belongs to live_result; no second state store or mixin is introduced.

PdkPreparation remains the sole lifecycle/state owner: selection context, jobs, ready catalogs, cache, cancellation events, pool registry and both locks. Collection helpers operate on individual checkpoint data; capture helpers receive one job/worker and explicit I/O functions; selection and quality helpers receive only required values or cache. No whole-host helper, mirrored state or forwarding property is introduced. Only the three policy constants are retained compatibility aliases. prepare/advance, details/captures and selection-prompt hook dispatch is preserved and tested; pdk_session keeps the current class entry.

SchematicSnapshotStore remains the sole owner of snapshot registry, SQLite connections, registration/commit/rollback and close. Schema validation, JSONL indexing, artifact I/O and query-value/text projection are stateless helpers with explicit values/connections; none receives the store or its registry. All store methods retain their behavior, with text projection receiving summary data rather than a resource-bearing snapshot object. The _import_sqlite injection point remains local. Only six schema/limit/error aliases are compatibility exports; the store is not scheduled for retirement.

Same-object compatibility exports only: executable qualification, Codex/Claude configuration, shared operational policy, terminal child environment and private home filesystem preparation have independent owners with explicit values. No owner object, forwarding wrapper/property or mirrored state is passed between modules. Existing controller/terminal_environment injection points remain unchanged; original __all__ is preserved. The six owners remain in the same package so relative executable resolution keeps its root. Bootstrap and gateway effects remain call-time, and the optional wrapper import stays lazy. Source-site managed skills link behavior is retained, not newly enabled for runtime distribution.
Owns asynchronous background request publication and closure; BackgroundJobs owns execution. AS-07C removed the reverse import alias from background_jobs.

RequestDispatcher keeps transport/runtime/workspace/timeout/live_session and the unknown-execution event; run_session retains every resource acquisition and cleanup branch and all original injection points. Extracted request source/result/artifact operations receive explicit paths, values, bounds and I/O callables, never the dispatcher or a new host. Its existing methods bind these dependencies and preserve override dispatch. The live recipe closure still selects current cancellation, runner and binding hooks at call time. The hash-only legacy accessor keeps its dynamic call to the old binding hook. Only listed helper/launch aliases are retained compatibility surfaces; lifecycle owners, method hooks and limits remain current. No property forwarding or duplicate state.

The original normalize and CLI remain canonical orchestration. Inspection schema/envelope validation, ordered symbol interface, complete connectivity cross-check and provenance have independent stateless owners. All 24 original definitions/constants retain their AST, including the long local connectivity algorithm and error paths. Reexports retain exact identity without wrappers or copied state; no repository monkeypatch consumer of old helper globals was found. The 341-line connectivity file retains one coherent bidirectional validation responsibility and local scratch indexes, avoiding a shared host/context object. Source search path registration enables existing alias checks for these private scripts only; it is not native inventory or runtime release approval.

The original main and netlist-cell loader remain canonical CLI input/report orchestration. Conservative SystemVerilog parsing and ModuleFacts, immutable Finding/severity values, conformance rules, and optional scratch-directory compilation each have one stateless owner. All 23 original definitions/constants preserve exact AST. Twenty-one helper/class/constant aliases retain exact owner identity, with no wrapper, shared host, copied state or reverse dependency. main still selects parser/checker hooks at call time. No existing repository consumer patches moved helper globals. Compiler source tests use deterministic process doubles to cover argument order, diagnostics, timeout and scratch cleanup; they do not qualify real xrun or runtime release. Private script helpers are not native build inputs.

Transcript composes the canonical Qt-independent ChatProjection with the Qt renderer. Event reduction, tool pairing and retention have one service implementation shared by live delivery and journal paging. Transcript owns only document/render state and presentation hooks. Renderer exports preserve the existing compatibility contract. The cohesive event reducer stays below the hard 500-line limit.
Workspace owns pane/widget state and closure. Tab geometry widgets and closing menu entries have their own class definitions, retained as same-object aliases at the old import path.
CatalogIndex owns incremental directory/catalog scans. SessionReader owns validated journal tail reads. Old reader/helper exports retain object identity; no reader cache is copied into the catalog.

Placement planning and preview retain their public entrypoints; tool schema, bounds and declarative options share one schema owner. All listed values are same-object aliases rather than copied schemas.
Relay orchestration retains the authenticated connection and wire handling. StdioLines alone owns the reader queue/thread and SKILL line assembly; error classes and reader remain same-object exports.

Maintenance retains lock acquisition, compression/publication/pruning order and its original failure-injection hooks. Archive record validation/paths have a single definition owner with explicitly retained aliases.

AuditService owns its pending mailboxes, lock scopes and durable send order. Question normalization, evidence/answer records and confirmed-choice checks receive explicit values or validators. Old policy/function exports retain exact object identity; deliver_local remains the existing provider operation.

ContextBroker owns listener/handshake and peer publication under its condition. Peer owns request mailboxes; BindingRegistry owns session request counts; registration, routing and dispatch take explicit protocol dependencies. The original request/dispatch hooks remain callable. Peer and call-scope aliases have the listed retirement conditions.

CodexBackend owns task admission, active/stale state, MCP admission and connection publication/close. TaskJournal owns event buffering/progress and task projections; per-task submission and per-turn consumption use explicit journal, thread binding and collaborator operations, never the whole backend. Runtime factories and the clock remain resolved through the old module hooks. Only the instruction value alias has a retirement condition.
